old: Its first half began as the word for a reddish, fire-colored hue, which somehow ended up naming a desk covering.
One half means "office," and it started life as the name of a coarse red cloth.
Like "democracy" and "autocracy," its second half comes from the Greek word for rule, kratos.
clues: This noun for a way of running large organizations traces back to a coarse reddish cloth that once covered writing desks.
More than mere paperwork, it is the whole system of officials and rigid rules running governments and big institutions, coined in French to mean rule by desks.
It shares its ending with democracy and autocracy, and people grumble about its red tape whenever a simple request takes six forms and three departments.
